of telecommunications services in all forms and modalities authorized by the legislation in force after applying for the relevant licenses as required by the regulatory framework, as well as the production, industrialization, processing,
commercialization, conditioning, transportation and stockpiling of grains and products derived from grains, as well as any other activity complementary to its industrial and commercial business or any activity which may be necessary to attain its
object. To better achieve these purposes, it may set up, become associated with or have an interest in any public or private entity domiciled in Argentina or abroad, within the limits set forth in the Bylaws. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>General information </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">YPF S.A. (&#147;YPF&#148;
or the &#147;Company&#148;) is a stock corporation (sociedad an&oacute;nima) incorporated under the Argentine laws, with a registered office at Macacha G&uuml;emes 515, in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">YPF and its subsidiaries (the &#147;Group&#148;) form the leading energy group in Argentina, which operates a fully integrated oil and gas chain with
leading market positions across the domestic Upstream, Midstream and Downstream, LNG and Integrated Gas and New Energies business segments (see Note 6). </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONDENSED INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.a) Applicable accounting framework </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The condensed interim
consolidated financial statements of the Company for the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, are presented in accordance with IAS 34 &#147;Interim financial reporting&#148;. Therefore, they should be read together with the annual
consolidated financial statements of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2024 (&#147;annual consolidated financial statements&#148;) presented in U.S. dollars and in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These condensed interim consolidated financial statements corresponding to the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025 are unaudited. The Company
believes they include all necessary adjustments to reasonably present the results of each period on a basis consistent with the audited annual consolidated financial statements. Net Income for the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025 does
not necessarily reflect the proportion of the Group&#146;s full-year net income. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.b) Material accounting policies </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The material accounting policies are described in Note 2.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The accounting policies adopted in the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used in the
preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, except for the valuation policy for income tax detailed in Note 19. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Functional
currency </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As mentioned in Note 2.b.1) to the annual consolidated financial statements, YPF has defined the U.S. dollar as its functional currency.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The consolidated financial statements used by YPF for statutory, legal and regulatory purposes in Argentina are those in pesos and filed with the CNV
and approved by the Board of Directors and authorized to be issued on May&nbsp;7, 2025. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Business combinations </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group analyzes whether the assets acquired and liabilities assumed in a transaction qualify as a business combination in accordance with IFRS 3
&#147;Business combinations&#148;. Business combinations are accounted for using the acquisition method, which requires, among others, the recognition and measurement at fair value of the identifiable assets acquired, the liabilities assumed and any
<FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-controlling</FONT> interest. The excess of the consideration transferred over such fair value is recognized as goodwill and the shortfall as a gain in profit or loss for the period. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">When the assets acquired are not a business, the Group accounts for the transaction as the acquisition of an asset. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Adoption of new standards and interpretations effective as from January&nbsp;1, 2025 </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Company has adopted all new and revised standards and interpretations, issued by the IASB, relevant to its operations which are of mandatory and
effective application as of March&nbsp;31, 2025, as described in Note 2.b.14) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Standards and
interpretations issued by the IASB whose application is not mandatory at the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and have not been adopted by the Group </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In accordance with Article 1, Chapter III, Title IV of the CNV rules, the early application of the IFRS and/or their amendments is not permitted for
issuers filing financial statements with the CNV, unless specifically admitted by such agency. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.c) Significant estimates and key sources of estimation
uncertainty </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In preparing the financial statements at a certain date, the Group is required to make estimates and assessments affecting the amount
of assets and liabilities recorded and the contingent assets and liabilities disclosed at such date, as well as income and expenses recognized in the fiscal year or period. Actual future profit or loss might differ from the estimates and assessments
made at the date of preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The assumptions relating to the future and other key
sources of uncertainty about the estimates made for the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used by the Group in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, which
are disclosed in Note 2.c) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>2.d) Comparative information </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Amounts and other financial information corresponding to the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2024 and for the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31,
2024 are an integral part of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and are intended to be read only in relation to these financial statements. Likewise, changes have been made to the comparative figures in Notes 6 and 26 as
mentioned in Note 6. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Historically, the Group&#146;s results have been subject to seasonal fluctuations throughout the year, particularly as a result of the increase in natural
gas sales during the winter driven by the increased demand in the residential segment. Consequently, the Group is subject to seasonal fluctuations in its sales volumes and prices, with higher sales of natural gas during the winter at higher prices.

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group&#146;s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: Market risk (including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk, and price risk),
liquidity risk and credit risk. Within the Group, risk management functions are conducted in relation to financial risks associated to financial instruments to which the Group is exposed during a certain period or as of a specific date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, there were no significant changes in the administration or policies of risk management
implemented by the Group as described in Note 4 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Liquidity risk management </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Most of the Group&#146;s loans contain market-standard covenants for contracts of this nature, which include financial covenants in respect of the
Group&#146;s leverage ratio and debt service coverage ratio, and events of defaults triggered by materially adverse judgements, among others. See Notes 17, 33 and 34 to the annual consolidated financial statements and Notes 18 and 34. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group monitors compliance with covenants on a quarterly basis. As of March&nbsp;31, 2025, the Group is in compliance with its covenants. </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B><A NAME="ex_1toc919767_13"></A>6.</B></TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL; " ALIGN="justify"><B>BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The different business segments in which the Group&#146;s organization is structured consider the different activities from which the Group can obtain
revenues and incur expenses. Such organizational structure is based on the way in which the chief decision maker analyzes the main operating and financial magnitudes for making decisions about resource allocation and performance assessment, also
considering the business strategy of the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Business segment information is presented consistently with the manner of reporting the information
used by the chief decision maker to allocate resources and assess business segment performance. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the current fiscal year, as a consequence of
the organizational structure changes in which the New Energies Vice Presidency was created and the Gas and Power Vice Presidency and the Downstream Vice Presidency were reformulated as the LNG and Integrated Gas Vice Presidency and the Midstream and
Downstream Vice Presidency, respectively, the complete management scope of these new business units was determined. On January&nbsp;1, 2025, these organizational changes resulted in a modification of the composition of the business segments
according to how the chief decision maker allocates resources and assesses the performance of these business segments, creating the New Energies business segment and readjusting the composition and definition of the businesses of the remaining
business segments. The changes in the business segments had no impact on the CGUs defined in Note 2.b.5) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As aforementioned and in Note 5 to the annual consolidated financial statements, the comparative information for the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31,
2024 and the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 has been restated. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The business segments structure is organized as follows: </P>
<P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">

<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Upstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Upstream business segment performs all activities related to the exploration and exploitation of hydrocarbon fields and production of
crude oil and natural gas. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;1, 2024, certain assets related to the production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking
purposes, which were formerly included in the Upstream business segment, were assigned to Central Administration and Others. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its
revenues are mainly derived from: (i)&nbsp;the sale of the produced crude oil to the Midstream and Downstream business segment; (ii)&nbsp;the sale of the produced natural gas to the LNG and Integrated Gas business segment; and (iii)&nbsp;the sale of
the natural gas retained in plant to the Midstream and Downstream business segment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned
activities. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:80pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt; margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Midstream and Downstream business segment performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;the refining, transportation and commercialization
of refined products; (ii)&nbsp;the production, transportation and commercialization of petrochemical products; (iii)&nbsp;the transportation and commercialization of crude oil; and (iv)&nbsp;the commercialization of specialties for the agribusiness
industry and of grains and their <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</FONT> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;1, 2025, as a consequence of
the organizational changes described above, the assets related to the natural gas transportation, the conditioning and processing of natural gas retained in plant for the separation and fractionation of gasoline, propane and butane, the storage of
the produced natural gas, and the commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminal in Escobar, which were formerly included in the Gas and Power business segment, were assigned to the Midstream and Downstream business segment.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the sale of crude oil, refined and petrochemical products, and specialties for agribusiness
industry and grains and their <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">by-products,</FONT> through the businesses of B2C (Retail), B2B (Commercial Networks, Industries, Transportation, Aviation, Agro, Lubricants and Specialties), LPG, Chemicals,
International Trade and Transportation and Sales to Companies. In addition, it obtains revenues from midstream oil, midstream gas and natural gas storage operations and the provision of LNG regasification services. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned activities, including the purchase of: (i)&nbsp;crude oil from the Upstream business
segment and third parties; (ii)&nbsp;natural gas to be consumed in the refinery and petrochemical industrial complexes from the LNG and Integrated Gas business segment; and (iii)&nbsp;natural gas retained in plant from the Upstream business segment.
</P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The LNG and Integrated Gas business segment performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;natural gas commercialization to third parties and to
the Midstream and Downstream business segment; (ii)&nbsp;the separation of natural gas liquids and their fractionation, storage and transportation for the production of ethane, propane, butane and gasoline, and its commercialization, through our
investment in joint venture Mega; and (iii)&nbsp;the development of LNG capacity. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;1, 2025, as a consequence of the
organizational changes described above, the assets related to the natural gas transportation, the conditioning and processing of natural gas retained in plant for the separation and fractionation of gasoline, propane and butane, the storage of the
produced natural gas, and the commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminal in Escobar, which were formerly included in the Gas and Power business segment, were assigned to the Midstream and Downstream business segment.
Furthermore, the assets related to the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy, and the production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers through
our investments in associates and joint ventures, which were formerly included in the Gas and Power business segment, were assigned to the New Energies business segment. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the commercialization of natural gas as producers to third parties and to the Midstream and
Downstream and the New Energies business segments. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned activities, including the

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;1, 2025, as a consequence of the organizational changes described above, the New Energies Vice Presidency was created and

electric power and renewable energy and the production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers through our investments in associates and joint ventures, which were formerly included in the Gas and Power business segment, were assigned to the
New Energies business segment. In addition, the assets related to the provision of research and development services of technology applied to the hydrocarbon industry through our subsidiary <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Y-TEC,</FONT> previously
included in Central Administration and Others, were assigned to the New Energies business segment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The New Energies business segment
performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;the definition and development of the new energy portfolio; (ii)&nbsp;the definition and development of sustainability and energy transitions programs; (iii)&nbsp;the distribution of natural gas through our
subsidiary Metrogas; and (iv)&nbsp;the provision of research and development services of technology applied to the hydrocarbon industry through our subsidiary <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">Y-TEC.</FONT> Furthermore, through our investments in
associates and joint ventures, the New Energies business segment performs activities related to: (i)&nbsp;the generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy; and (ii)&nbsp;the production, storage, distribution and sale of
fertilizers. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the sale of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned activities, including the purchase of natural gas from the LNG and Integrated Gas
business segment. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It includes the remaining activities performed by the Group that do not fall within the aforementioned business segments and which are not

Energies business segment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Sales between business segments were made at internal transfer prices established by the Group, which approximately
reflect domestic market prices. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Operating profit or loss and assets of each business segment have been determined after consolidation adjustments.

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>12. ASSETS HELD FOR SALE AND ASSOCIATED LIABILITIES (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;31, 2025, after the fulfillment of all the closing conditions by YPF and PECOM, the
transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF in such exploitation concessions in favor of PECOM was formalized. In the context of this transaction, YPF received 28. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2025, based on the closing of the aforementioned assignment agreements for the &#147;Estaci&oacute;n Fern&aacute;ndez Oro&#148;, and
&#147;Campamento Central - Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Perdido&#148; exploitation concessions and considering the fair value less costs to sell of such groups of assets, the result from the sale of such assets did not have significant effects.
Additionally, the derecognition of the carrying amount of net assets held for sale and liabilities directly associated with assets held for sale related to such exploitation concessions was 45 as of such date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The assignment agreements that have met the agreed closing conditions as of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial
statements, for which the transaction was settled after the end of the period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, are described below. Consequently, the disposal of these groups of assets as held for sale did not meet the requirements of IFRS 5 to recognize
their sale at the end of the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, and therefore these groups of assets continue to be classified as held for sale as of that date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Barrancas, Vizcacheras, La Ventana, Ceferino, Mesa Verde and R&iacute;o Tunuy&aacute;n </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;29, 2025, Resolution No.&nbsp;16/2025 was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Mendoza, which authorized the transfer of
100% of YPF&#146;s rights and obligations in &#147;Barrancas&#148;, &#147;Vizcacheras&#148;, &#147;La Ventana&#148;, &#147;Ceferino&#148;, &#147;Mesa Verde&#148; and &#147;R&iacute;o Tunuy&aacute;n&#148; exploitation concessions in favor of
Petr&oacute;leos Sudamericanos S.A. (&#147;PS&#148;). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On March&nbsp;27, 2025, after the fulfillment of all the closing conditions by YPF and PS, the
transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF in such exploitation concessions in favor of PS was formalized with effective date as of April&nbsp;1, 2025. In the context of this transaction, YPF received 3 and, in addition, contemplates
crude oil deliveries for a period of 2 years as payment in kind. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">At the closing date of the aforementioned assignment agreements for the
&#147;Barrancas&#148;, &#147;Vizcacheras&#148;, &#147;La Ventana&#148;, &#147;Ceferino&#148;, &#147;Mesa Verde&#148; and &#147;R&iacute;o Tunuy&aacute;n&#148; exploitation concessions and considering the fair value less costs to sell of such groups
of assets, the result from the sale of such assets amounts to a gain of 78. Additionally, the derecognition of the carrying amount of net liabilities directly associated with assets held for sale and assets held for sale related to such exploitation
concessions is 31. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In addition, at the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the following assignment
agreements, although they have been formally resolved by the corresponding enforcement authorities, are subject to the fulfillment of closing conditions: </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Se&ntilde;al Cerro Bayo, Volc&aacute;n Auca Mahuida, Don Ruiz and Las Manadas </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;7, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;372/2025 was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n, which authorized the transfer of
100% of YPF&#146;s rights and obligations in &#147;Se&ntilde;al Cerro Bayo&#148;, &#147;Volc&aacute;n Auca Mahuida&#148;, &#147;Don Ruiz&#148; and &#147;Las Manadas&#148; exploitation concessions in favor of Bentia Energy S.A. (&#147;Bentia&#148;)
and Ingenier&iacute;a SIMA S.A. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the assignment agreement is subject to the fulfillment of closing conditions. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Al Norte de la Dorsal and Oct&oacute;gono </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On
April&nbsp;9, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;380/2025 was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n, which authorized the transfer of 100% of YPF&#146;s rights and obligations in &#147;Al Norte de la Dorsal&#148; and
&#147;Oct&oacute;gono&#148; exploitation concessions in favor of Bentia. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the assignment agreement is subject to the fulfillment of closing conditions. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Company has signed assignment agreements for certain groups
of assets as held for sale that are subject to closing conditions mainly related to regulatory and provincial approvals, for which the Company is taking the necessary steps to close; and it is highly probable that these assets will be disposed. In
addition, the Company maintains groups of assets as held for sale for which agreements have not yet been signed but continues in negotiations with third parties for their disposal or reversal. The delay in the fulfillment of the plan for the
disposal of mature fields is due to the complexity of the negotiations, which is beyond the Company&#146;s control. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Company considers that the disposal of
such assets continues to be highly probable during 2025. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:60pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>12. ASSETS HELD FOR SALE AND ASSOCIATED LIABILITIES (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Accounting matters </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Considering that the assets classified as held for sale are measured at the lower of their carrying amount and fair value less costs to
sell (&#147;fair value&#148;), the Company evaluates the changes in fair value, recognizing a profit up to the limit of the impairment loss previously recognized or an impairment loss in addition to that previously recognized for such changes, (see
Note 2.b.13) to the annual consolidated financial statement). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">For the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, based on the
aforementioned evaluation of the changes in the fair value, the Company recognized a loss due to changes in the fair value of assets held for sale of 200 in the &#147;Other net operating results&#148; line item in the statement of comprehensive
income, mainly generated by higher costs associated with expenses of different nature that are expected to arise related to the assets in connection with the ongoing negotiations progress. The carrying amount of the assets held for sale may be
adjusted in future periods depending on the results of the disposal process carry out by YPF and the economic consideration to be agreed with third parties for such assets. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In relation to the Company&#146;s own personnel, the Company recognized for the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025 a charge for
severance indemnities of 26 in the &#147;Provision for severance indemnities&#148; line under &#147;Other operating results, net&#148; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. </P>

IAS 34, income tax expense is recognized in each interim period based on the best estimate of the effective income tax rate expected as of the closing date of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, considering the tax criteria
that the Group assumes to apply during the fiscal year. If the estimate of such rate is modified based on new elements of judgment, the income tax expense could require adjustments in subsequent periods. </P>

Note 2.c) &#147;Income tax and deferred taxes&#148; section to the annual consolidated financial statements), and its effects, are described in Note 18 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="ex_1toc919767_39"></A>32. SHAREHOLDERS&#146; EQUITY </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2025, the Company&#146;s capital amounts to 3,922 and treasury shares amount to 11 represented by 393,312,793 book-entry shares of
common stock and divided into four classes of shares (A, B, C and D), with a par value of 10 pesos and 1 vote per share. These shares are fully subscribed, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">paid-in</FONT> and authorized for stock exchange listing.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2025, there are 3,764 Class&nbsp;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&nbsp;A share remains outstanding, the affirmative
vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&nbsp;mergers; (ii) acquisitions of more than 50% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&nbsp;transfers of all the YPF&#146;s exploitation and exploration rights; (iv)&nbsp;the voluntary
dissolution of YPF; (v)&nbsp;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina; or (vi)&nbsp;make an acquisition that would result in the purchaser holding 15% or more of the Company&#146;s capital stock, or 20% or more of the outstanding
Class&nbsp;D shares. Items (iii)&nbsp;and (iv) also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month periods ended
March&nbsp;31, 2025 and 2024, the Company has not repurchased any of its own shares. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;30, 2025, the General Shareholders&#146; Meeting
was held, which approved the statutory financial statements of YPF (see Note 2.b)) corresponding to the year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2024 and, additionally, approved the following in relation to the retained earnings: (i)&nbsp;completely
disaffect the reserve for purchase of treasury shares and the reserve for investments; (ii)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 34,205&nbsp;million of pesos (US$ 33 million) to constitute a reserve for purchase of treasury shares; and (iii)&nbsp;allocate
the amount of 6,787,343&nbsp;million of pesos (US$ 6,587 million) to constitute a reserve for investments. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="ex_1toc919767_40"></A>33. EARNINGS PER SHARE

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>35. CONTRACTUAL COMMITMENTS (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In order to supply the FLNG Hilli and FLNG MKII vessels with natural gas for the liquefaction process,
SESA entered into natural gas supply agreements (&#147;GSA&#148;) with PAE, Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas, Pampa and Wintershall for the term of 20 years (see Note 36.f)). In this regard, in order for both vessels to operate all year round,
SESA contemplates the construction of a dedicated gas pipeline between the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n and the San Mat&iacute;as Gulf in the Province of R&iacute;o Negro. Operations of the FLNG Hilli vessel are expected to commence in late 2027 or
early 2028 and those of the FLNG MKII vessel are expected to commence in late 2028. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim
consolidated financial statements, the shareholding in SESA is as follows: PAE (30%), Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas (25%), Pampa (20%), Wintershall (15%) and Golar Subholding (10%). The Company has entered into the GSA and the SESA
Shareholders&#146; Agreement guaranteeing the obligations of its subsidiary Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas under such agreements. In addition, the Company will grant guarantees in favor of Golar Hilli Corporation for up to 137.5 and in favor of
Golar MKII Corporation for up to 187.5 representing 25% of Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas&#146; equity interest in SESA. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><I>The dates indicated

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">ENARGAS, through several resolutions, approved the transition tariff schemes to be applied by Metrogas until the rates resulting from the RQT came into

corresponding to Metrogas effective as from May&nbsp;1, 2025. The increase expected as a result of the RQT process will be effective in 31 consecutive monthly increases, which recognizes a cost for the deferral at a real weighted average cost of the
capital employed rate in pesos of 7.64% and establishes that the increase in distribution tariffs for May 2025 applicable to residential users and general service customers will be 3%. The application of the remaining increase derived from the RQT
will be completed in the remaining 30 installments, plus the recognition of the cost of the aforementioned deferral. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:60pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<TD VALIGN="top"><FONT STYLE="font-size:10pt"><B>YPF SOCIEDAD ANONIMA</B></FONT></TD>
<TD VALIGN="bottom">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD VALIGN="top"></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt">
<TD VALIGN="top" COLSPAN="5"> <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>NOTES TO THE CONDENSED INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:1pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>AS OF MARCH 31, 2025 AND COMPARATIVE INFORMATION</B></P></TD></TR>
<TR STYLE="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt">
<TD VALIGN="top" COLSPAN="5">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except for shares and per share amounts expressed in United States dollars, or as otherwise indicated)</TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36. MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.h) Custom regulations </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.g) to the
annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.i) Regulations related to the Foreign Exchange Market </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.h) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the three-month period ended
March&nbsp;31, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;11, 2025, the Argentine Government announced measures to loosen the foreign exchange regime
and reinforce the monetary framework. By virtue of this, the BCRA implemented a new foreign exchange regime in which certain restrictions to access the Foreign Exchange Market were eliminated. The following are the main measures: (i)&nbsp;the
&#147;crawling peg&#148; adjustment mechanism is eliminated and the dollar exchange rate in the Foreign Exchange Market may fluctuate in a range between 1,000 pesos and 1,400 pesos, whose limits will be increased at a rate of 1% per month;
(ii)&nbsp;the &#147;blend&#148; dollar was eliminated (see Note 36.i) &#147;Export Increase Program&#148; section); (iii) certain foreign exchange restrictions to individuals for the purchase of foreign currency were eliminated; (iv)&nbsp;access to
the Foreign Exchange Market is allowed without prior approval of the BCRA for the payment of dividends to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-resident</FONT> shareholders accrued as from fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2025; and
(v)&nbsp;the terms for the payment of foreign trade transactions are flexibilized, eliminating the schedule established by the BCRA for access to the Foreign Exchange Market without prior approval for the payment of imports of goods with customs
entry registration as from December&nbsp;13, 2023 and of services rendered and/or accrued as from such date. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The aforementioned measures adopted by
the Argentine Government will be financially supported by a new Extended Facilities Facility (&#147;EFF&#148;) agreed with the International Monetary Fund (&#147;IMF&#148;). In this regard, on March&nbsp;11, 2025, through DNU No.&nbsp;179/2025, the
PEN approved to enter into a new EFF with the IMF, which was approved by the Chamber of Deputies of the Argentine Congress on March&nbsp;19, 2025. On April&nbsp;8 and April&nbsp;11, 2025, the IMF and the Argentine Government, respectively, announced
that they had reached an agreement on a comprehensive economic program based on a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">4-year</FONT> EFF for a total of US$ 20&nbsp;billion, which includes quarterly reviews of targets. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Export Increase Program </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;14, 2025,
Decree No.&nbsp;269/2025 repealed the Export Increase Program and as from such date the proceeds from the export of goods and services, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-export</FONT> financings, post- export financings and advance payments must
be settled 100% through the Foreign Exchange Market within a general term of 20 days. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.j) Decree of Necessity and Urgency (&#147;DNU&#148; by its acronym in
Spanish) No.&nbsp;70/2023 </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework
described in Note 36.i) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>36.k) Law of Bases and Starting Points for the Freedom of Argentines No.&nbsp;27,742
(&#147;Bases Law&#148;) and Regulatory Decree No 1,057/2024 (&#147;Decree No 1,057/2024&#148;) </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31,
2025, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.j) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><I>The dates indicated
correspond to the date of publication in the respective Official Gazettes, unless otherwise indicated. </I></P> <P STYLE="font-size:60pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>37. BALANCES AND TRANSACTIONS WITH RELATED PARTIES (cont.) </B></P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Additionally, the Group has entered into certain financing and insurance transactions with entities
related to the national public sector. Such transactions consist of certain financial transactions that are described in Notes 16, 17 and 23 and transactions with Naci&oacute;n Seguros S.A. related to certain insurance policies contracts. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2025, the Group holds Bonds of the Argentine Republic 2029 and 2030, BCRA bonds (BOPREAL, for its acronym in spanish) and bills
issued by the National Government identified as investments in financial assets (see Note 16). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In addition, in connection with the investment

the three-month periods ended March&nbsp;31, 2025 and 2024, YPF and CHNC carried out transactions such as the purchases of crude oil by YPF for 133 and 115, respectively, among others. These transactions were consummated in accordance with the
general and regulatory conditions of the market. The net balance payable to CHNC as of March&nbsp;31, 2025 and December&nbsp;31, 2024 amounts to 53 and 85, respectively. See Note 37 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>

</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Short-term benefit programs</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31,

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with the remaining share-based benefit plans was 2 and 1 to be settled in equity instruments, for the

<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;9, 2025, the Company issued additional Class&nbsp;XXX NO for 204 maturing in July 2026 at an issue price of 96.5% of nominal value. The
integration of additional Class&nbsp;XXX NO was made in kind through the delivery of Class&nbsp;XXIII NO for 39 and in cash for 165. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On May&nbsp;6,
2025, the Company announced the results of the tender of the Class&nbsp;XXXVII NO denominated and payable in U.S. dollars maturing in May 2027, having accepted offers for 140 at a fixed nominal annual interest rate of 7%. The Class&nbsp;XXXVII NO
will be issued and integrated in U.S. dollars on May&nbsp;7, 2025. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;2, 2025, a Memorandum of Understanding (&#147;MOU&#148;) was signed
with the Province of Santa Cruz and Fomicruz S.E. for the purpose of establishing the general terms and conditions upon which the assignment to the latter of the exploitation concessions &#147;Cerro Piedra - Cerro Guadal Norte&#148;, &#147;Barranca
Yankowsky&#148;, &#147;Los Monos&#148;, &#147;El Guadal - Lomas del Cuy&#148;, &#147;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Vasco&#148;, &#147;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Yatel&#148;, &#147;Pico Truncado - El Cord&oacute;n&#148;, &#147;Los Perales - Las Mesetas&#148;,
&#147;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Le&oacute;n - Meseta Espinosa&#148;, &#147;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n de la Escondida - Las Heras&#148; and the transportation concessions associated with such concessions will be negotiated. The MOU, subject to the approval
by YPF&#146;s Board of Directors and the issuance of the corresponding provincial decree, was approved by YPF&#146;s Board of Directors on April&nbsp;9, 2025, and issued Provincial Decree No.&nbsp;376/2025 on May&nbsp;6, 2025. </P>

applying for the relevant licenses as required by the regulatory framework, as well as the production, industrialization, processing, commercialization, conditioning, transportation and stockpiling of grains and products derived from grains, as well

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="ex_2919767_8"></A>1. GENERAL INFORMATION, STRUCTURE AND ORGANIZATION OF THE GROUP&#146;S
BUSINESS </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>General information</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">YPF S.A.
(&#147;YPF&#148; or the &#147;Company&#148;) is a stock corporation<I> </I>(s<I>ociedad an&oacute;nima</I>) incorporated under the Argentine laws, with a registered office at Macacha G&uuml;emes 515, in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">YPF and its subsidiaries (the &#147;Group&#148;) form the leading energy group in Argentina, which operates a fully integrated oil and gas chain with
leading market positions across the domestic Upstream, Midstream and Downstream LNG and Integrated Gas and New Energies business segments (see Note 6). </P>

CONDENSED INTERIM CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.a) Applicable accounting framework </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The condensed interim consolidated financial statements of the Company for the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, are presented in accordance
with IAS 34 &#147;Interim financial reporting&#148;. Therefore, they should be read together with the annual consolidated financial statements of the Company as of December&nbsp;31, 2024 (&#147;annual consolidated financial statements&#148;)
presented in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards as issued by the IASB. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Moreover, some additional information required by the LGS and/or
CNV&#146;s Rules have been included. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These condensed interim consolidated financial statements corresponding to the three-month period ended
March&nbsp;31, 2025, are unaudited. The Company believes they include all necessary adjustments to reasonably present the results of each period on a basis consistent with the audited annual consolidated financial statements. Net Income for the
three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025 does not necessarily reflect the proportion of the Group&#146;s full-year net income. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.b) Material
accounting policies </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The material accounting policies are described in Note 2.b) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The accounting policies adopted in the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used in the
preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, except for the valuation policy for income tax detailed in Note 19. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Functional and
presentation currency</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As mentioned in Note 2.b.1) to the annual consolidated financial statements, YPF has defined the U.S. dollar as its
functional currency. Additionally, in accordance with the provisions of the LGS and the CNV rules, the Company must present its financial statements in pesos. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Business combinations</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group analyzes
whether the assets acquired and liabilities assumed in a transaction qualify as a business combination in accordance with IFRS 3 &#147;Business combinations&#148;. Business combinations are accounted for using the acquisition method, which requires,
among others, the recognition and measurement at fair value of the identifiable assets acquired, the liabilities assumed and any <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-controlling</FONT> interest. The excess of the consideration transferred over such
fair value is recognized as goodwill and the shortfall as a gain in profit or loss for the period. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">When the assets acquired are not a business, the
Group accounts for the transaction as the acquisition of an asset. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P> <P STYLE="font-size:60pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.c) Significant estimates and key sources of estimation uncertainty </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In preparing the financial statements at a certain date, the Group is required to make estimates and assessments affecting the amount of assets and

date of preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The assumptions relating to the future and other key sources of
uncertainty about the estimates made for the preparation of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements are consistent with those used by the Group in the preparation of the annual consolidated financial statements, which are disclosed
in Note 2.c) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>2.d) Comparative information </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Amounts and other financial information corresponding to the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2024 and for the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31,
2024 are an integral part of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements and are intended to be read only in relation to these financial statements. Likewise, changes have been made to the comparative figures in Notes 6 and 26 as
mentioned in Note 6. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B><A NAME="ex_2919767_10"></A>3. &#8201;SEASONALITY OF OPERATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Historically, the Group&#146;s results have been subject to seasonal fluctuations throughout the year, particularly as a result of the increase in natural
gas sales during the winter driven by the increased demand in the residential segment. Consequently, the Group is subject to seasonal fluctuations in its sales volumes and prices, with higher sales of natural gas during the winter at higher prices.

<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The most relevant acquisitions and disposals of companies that took place during the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025 are described below:

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="ex_2919767_12"></A>5. FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group&#146;s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: Market risk (including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk, and price risk),
liquidity risk and credit risk. Within the Group, risk management functions are conducted in relation to financial risks associated to financial instruments to which the Group is exposed during a certain period or as of a specific date. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, there were no significant changes in the administration or policies of risk management
implemented by the Group as described in Note 4 to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Liquidity risk management </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Most of the Group&#146;s loans contain market-standard covenants for contracts of this nature, which include financial covenants in respect of the
Group&#146;s leverage ratio and debt service coverage ratio, and events of defaults triggered by materially adverse judgements, among others. See Notes 17, 33 and 34 to the annual consolidated financial statements and Notes 18 and 34. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Group monitors compliance with covenants on a quarterly basis. As of March&nbsp;31, 2025, the Group is in compliance with its covenants. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B><A NAME="ex_2919767_13"></A>6. BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The different business segments in which the Group&#146;s organization is structured consider the different activities from which the Group can obtain
revenues and incur expenses. Such organizational structure is based on the way in which the chief decision maker analyzes the main operating and financial magnitudes for making decisions about resource allocation and performance assessment, also
considering the business strategy of the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Business segment information is presented in U.S. dollars, the functional currency of the Company
(see Note 2.b)), consistently with the manner of reporting the information used by the chief decision maker to allocate resources and assess business segment performance. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the current fiscal year, as a consequence of the organizational structure changes in which the New Energies Vice Presidency was created, and the Gas
and Power Vice Presidency and the Downstream Vice Presidency were reformulated as the LNG and Integrated Gas Vice Presidency and the Midstream and Downstream Vice Presidency respectively, the complete management scope of these new business units was
determined. On January&nbsp;1, 2025, these organizational changes resulted in a modification of the composition of the business segments according to how the chief decision maker allocates resources and assesses the performance of these business
segments, creating the New Energies business segment and readjusting the composition and definition of the businesses of the remaining business segments. The changes in the business segments had no impact on the CGUs defined in Note 2.b.5) to the
annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As aforementioned and in Note 5 to the annual consolidated financial statements, the comparative
information for the fiscal year ended December&nbsp;31, 2024 and the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2024 has been restated. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The business
segments structure is organized as follows: </P> <P STYLE="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE STYLE="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt" BORDER="0" CELLPADDING="0" CELLSPACING="0" WIDTH="100%">
<TR style = "page-break-inside:avoid">
<TD WIDTH="2%" VALIGN="top" ALIGN="left"><B>&#149;</B></TD>
<TD WIDTH="1%" VALIGN="top">&nbsp;</TD>
<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="justify" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Upstream </B></P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The Upstream business segment performs all activities related to the exploration and exploitation of hydrocarbon fields and production of
crude oil and natural gas. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On July&nbsp;1, 2024, certain assets related to the production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking
purposes, which were formerly included in the Upstream business segment, were assigned to Central Administration and Others. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Its
revenues are mainly derived from: (i)&nbsp;the sale of the produced crude oil to the Midstream and Downstream business segment; (ii)&nbsp;the sale of the produced natural gas to the LNG and Integrated Gas business segment; and (iii)&nbsp;the sale of
the natural gas retained in plant to the Midstream and Downstream business segment. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">It incurs all costs related to the aforementioned
activities. </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Description of the Mature Fields Project</B> </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The assignment agreements that have met the agreed closing conditions during the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, and therefore the
transaction was settled are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Estaci&oacute;n Fern&aacute;ndez Oro</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On December&nbsp;19, 2024, Decree No.&nbsp;525/2024 was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of R&iacute;o Negro, which authorized the
transfer of 100% of YPF&#146;s rights and obligations in the &#147;Estaci&oacute;n Fern&aacute;ndez Oro&#148; exploitation concession in favor of Quintana E&amp;P Argentina S.R.L., Quintana Energy Investments S.A., and Gas Storage and Midstream
Services S.A. (&#147;Quintana Consortium&#148;). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On February&nbsp;3, 2025, after the fulfillment of all the closing conditions by YPF and Quintana
Consortium, the transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF in such exploitation concessions in favor of Quintana Consortium was formalized. In the context of this transaction, YPF received US$ 23&nbsp;million. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Campamento Central-Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Perdido</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;6, 2025, Decree No.&nbsp;1,892/2024 was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Chubut, which authorized the transfer of 100%
of the rights and obligations in the &#147;Campamento Central - Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Perdido&#148; exploitation concession, in which YPF held a working interest of 50%, in favor of PECOM. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;31, 2025, after the fulfillment of all the closing conditions by YPF and PECOM, the transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF
in such exploitation concessions in favor of PECOM was formalized. In the context of this transaction, YPF received US$ 28&nbsp;million. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of
March&nbsp;31, 2025, based on the closing of the aforementioned assignment agreements for the &#147;Estaci&oacute;n Fern&aacute;ndez Oro&#148;, and &#147;Campamento Central - Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Perdido&#148; exploitation concessions and
considering the fair value less costs to sell of such groups of assets, the result from the sale of such assets did not have significant effects. Additionally, the derecognition of the carrying amount of net assets held for sale and liabilities
directly associated with assets held for sale related to such exploitation concessions was 46,580 as of such date. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Barrancas, Vizcacheras, La Ventana, Ceferino, Mesa Verde and R&iacute;o Tunuy&aacute;n</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;29, 2025, Resolution No.&nbsp;16/2025 was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Mendoza, which authorized the transfer of
100% of YPF&#146;s rights and obligations in &#147;Barrancas&#148;, &#147;Vizcacheras&#148;, &#147;La Ventana&#148;, &#147;Ceferino&#148;, &#147;Mesa Verde&#148; and &#147;R&iacute;o Tunuy&aacute;n&#148; exploitation concessions in favor of

contemplates crude oil deliveries for a period of 2 years as payment in kind. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">At the closing date of the aforementioned assignment agreements for the
&#147;Barrancas&#148;, &#147;Vizcacheras&#148;, &#147;La Ventana&#148;, &#147;Ceferino&#148;, &#147;Mesa Verde&#148; and &#147;R&iacute;o Tunuy&aacute;n&#148; exploitation concessions and considering the fair value less costs to sell of such groups
of assets, the result from the sale of such assets amounts to a gain of 83,634. Additionally, the derecognition of the carrying amount of net liabilities directly associated with assets held for sale and assets held for sale related to such
exploitation concessions is 33,248. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In addition, at the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the following
assignment agreements, although they have been formally resolved by the corresponding enforcement authorities, are subject to the fulfillment of closing conditions: </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Se&ntilde;al Cerro Bayo, Volc&aacute;n Auca Mahuida, Don Ruiz and Las Manadas</U> </P>

and Ingenier&iacute;a SIMA S.A. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the assignment agreement is subject to the fulfillment of closing conditions. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Al Norte de la Dorsal and Oct&oacute;gono</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On

&#147;Oct&oacute;gono&#148; exploitation concessions in favor of Bentia. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the assignment agreement is subject to the fulfillment of closing conditions. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Company has signed assignment agreements for certain groups
of assets as held for sale that are subject to closing conditions mainly related to regulatory and provincial approvals, for which the Company is taking the necessary steps to close; and it is highly probable that these assets will be disposed. In
addition, the Company maintains groups of assets as held for sale for which agreements have not yet been signed but continues in negotiations with third parties for their disposal or reversal. The delay in the fulfillment of the plan for the
disposal of mature fields is due to the complexity of the negotiations, which is beyond the Company&#146;s control. As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, the Company considers that the disposal of
such assets continues to be highly probable during 2025. </P>

<TD ALIGN="left" VALIGN="top"> <P ALIGN="left" STYLE=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt"><B>Accounting matters</B> </P></TD></TR></TABLE>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Considering that the assets classified as held for sale are measured at the lower of their carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell (&#147;fair
value&#148;), the Company evaluates the changes in fair value, recognizing a profit up to the limit of the impairment loss previously recognized or an impairment loss in addition to that previously recognized for such changes, (see Note 2.b.13) to
the annual consolidated financial statement). </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">For the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, based on the aforementioned evaluation of the
changes in the fair value, the Company recognized a loss due to changes in the fair value of assets held for sale of 214,500 in the &#147;Other net operating results&#148; line item in the statement of comprehensive income, mainly generated by
higher costs associated with expenses of different nature that are expected to arise related to the assets in connection with the ongoing negotiations progress. The carrying amount of the assets held for sale may be adjusted in future periods
depending on the results of the disposal process carry out by YPF and the economic consideration to be agreed with third parties for such assets. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In
relation to the Company&#146;s own personnel, the Company recognized for the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025 a charge for severance indemnities of 28,026 in the &#147;Provision for severance indemnities&#148; line under &#147;Other
operating results, net&#148; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL"><B>13. INVENTORIES </B></P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>32. SHAREHOLDERS&#146; EQUITY </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2025, the Company&#146;s capital amounts to 3,922 and treasury shares amount to 11 represented by 393,312,793 book-entry shares of
common stock and divided into four classes of shares (A, B, C and D), with a par value of 10 pesos and 1 vote per share. These shares are fully subscribed, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">paid-in</FONT> and authorized for stock exchange listing.
</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2025, there are 3,764 Class&nbsp;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&nbsp;A share remains outstanding, the affirmative
vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&nbsp;mergers; (ii) acquisitions of more than 50% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&nbsp;transfers of all the YPF&#146;s exploitation and exploration rights; (iv)&nbsp;the voluntary
dissolution of YPF; (v)&nbsp;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina; or (vi)&nbsp;make an acquisition that would result in the purchaser holding 15% or more of the Company&#146;s capital stock, or 20% or more of the outstanding
Class&nbsp;D shares. Items (iii)&nbsp;and (iv) also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month periods ended
March&nbsp;31, 2025 and 2024, the Company has not repurchased any of its own shares. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;30, 2025, the General Shareholders&#146; Meeting
was held, which approved the statutory financial statements of YPF (see Note 2.b)) corresponding to the year ended on December&nbsp;31, 2024 and, additionally, approved the following in relation to the retained earnings: (i)&nbsp;completely
disaffect the reserve for purchase of treasury shares and the reserve for investments; (ii)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 34,205 to constitute a reserve for purchase of treasury shares; and (iii)&nbsp;allocate the amount of 6,787,343 to constitute a
reserve for investments. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>33. EARNINGS PER SHARE </B></P>

<p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">In order to supply the FLNG Hilli and FLNG MKII vessels with natural gas for the liquefaction process,
SESA entered into natural gas supply agreements (&#147;GSA&#148;) with PAE, Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas, Pampa and Wintershall for the term of 20 years (see Note 36.f)). In this regard, in order for both vessels to operate all year round,
SESA contemplates the construction of a dedicated gas pipeline between the Province of Neuqu&eacute;n and the San Mat&iacute;as Gulf in the Province of R&iacute;o Negro. Operations of the FLNG Hilli vessel are expected to commence in late 2027 or
early 2028 and those of the FLNG MKII vessel are expected to commence in late 2028. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim
consolidated financial statements, the shareholding in SESA is as follows: PAE (30%), Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas (25%), Pampa (20%), Wintershall (15%) and Golar Subholding (10%). The Company has entered into the GSA and the SESA
Shareholders&#146; Agreement guaranteeing the obligations of its subsidiary Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas under such agreements. In addition, the Company will grant guarantees in favor of Golar Hilli Corporation for up to US$ 137.5&nbsp;million
and in favor of Golar MKII Corporation for up to US$ 187.5&nbsp;million representing 25% of Sur Inversiones Energ&eacute;ticas&#146; equity interest in SESA. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36. MAIN REGULATIONS </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.a) Regulations
