regulatory framework described in Note 36.a) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.b) Regulations applicable to the Midstream and
Downstream business segment </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, there were no significant updates to the regulatory
framework described in Notes&nbsp;36.b), 36.c.1), 36.c.2) &#147;LNG&#148; section and 36.c.4) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.c) Regulations applicable to the LNG and Integrated Gas business segment </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Notes 36.c.1) and
36.c.2) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.d) Regulations applicable to the New Energies business segment </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Notes 36.c.3), 36.c.5) and 36.c.6) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the three-month
period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.d.1) Regulatory requirements applicable to natural gas distribution </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>Tariff schemes and tariff renegotiations </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">ENARGAS, through
several resolutions, approved the transition tariff schemes to be applied by Metrogas until the rates resulting from the RQT came into force in accordance with the provisions of Decree No.&nbsp;55/2023. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;30, 2025, ENARGAS Resolution No.&nbsp;257/2025 was published, which approved: (i)&nbsp;the RQT corresponding to Metrogas; (ii)&nbsp;the
segmentation of residential users; (iii)&nbsp;the investment plans for the five-year period 2025 - 2030; and (iv)&nbsp;the initial tariff scheme and the schemes of rates and charges corresponding to Metrogas effective as from May&nbsp;1, 2025. The
increase expected as a result of the RQT process will be effective in 31 consecutive monthly increases, which recognizes a cost for the deferral at a real weighted average cost of the capital employed rate in pesos of 7.64% and establishes that the
increase in distribution tariffs for May 2025 applicable to residential users and general service customers will be 3%. The application of the remaining increase derived from the RQT will be completed in the remaining 30 installments, plus the
recognition of the cost of the aforementioned deferral. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Procedure for the compensation of the lower revenues received by natural gas distributors from their
users</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On January&nbsp;31, 2025, SE Resolution No.&nbsp;24/2025 repealed as from February&nbsp;1, 2025 MINEM Resolution No. <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">508-E/2017,</FONT> which established the procedure to compensate natural gas distributors for lower revenues due to benefits and/or bonuses and higher costs of UNG and unified the compensation mechanisms for lower revenues
received as a consequence of the application of incentive programs involving bonuses on the price of natural gas in the PIST. The amounts to be compensated will be deducted from the amounts to be paid by distributors to natural gas producers and
will be directly compensated by the SE through the Plan GasAr 2023-2028. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.d.2) Regulatory framework associated with electric power generation
</B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL"><U>CAMMESA </U></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The SE, through complementary notes to SE
Resolution No.&nbsp;21/2025, informed to CAMMESA of the &#147;Guidelines for the Standardization of the MEM and its Progressive Adaptation&#148;, which detail the modifications foreseen for the management of fuels, the determination of prices and
the operation of the term market and the spot market are detailed. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.e) Incentive programs for hydrocarbon production </B></P>

March&nbsp;31, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.e.1) Incentive programs for natural gas production </B></P>

Transportation System for all Hydrocarbon Basins in the Country 2023-2028 (&#147;Plan GasAr 2023-2028&#148;)</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The SE, through several resolutions,
approves the natural gas prices at the PIST to be passed-through to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">end-users</FONT> in connection with current contracts entered into within the framework of the Plan GasAr 2023-2028. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.h) Custom regulations </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.g) to the
annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.i) Regulations related to the Foreign Exchange Market </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.h) to the annual consolidated financial statements for the three-month period ended
March&nbsp;31, 2025, are described below: </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;11, 2025, the Argentine Government announced measures to loosen the foreign exchange regime
and reinforce the monetary framework. By virtue of this, the BCRA implemented a new foreign exchange regime in which certain restrictions to access the Foreign Exchange Market were eliminated. The following are the main measures: (i)&nbsp;the
&#147;crawling peg&#148; adjustment mechanism is eliminated and the dollar exchange rate in the Foreign Exchange Market may fluctuate in a range between 1,000 pesos and 1,400 pesos, whose limits will be increased at a rate of 1% per month;
(ii)&nbsp;the &#147;blend&#148; dollar was eliminated (see Note 36.i) &#147;Export Increase Program&#148; section); (iii) certain foreign exchange restrictions to individuals for the purchase of foreign currency were eliminated; (iv)&nbsp;access to
the Foreign Exchange Market is allowed without prior approval of the BCRA for the payment of dividends to <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-resident</FONT> shareholders accrued as from fiscal years beginning on or after January&nbsp;1, 2025; and
(v)&nbsp;the terms for the payment of foreign trade transactions are flexibilized, eliminating the schedule established by the BCRA for access to the Foreign Exchange Market without prior approval for the payment of imports of goods with customs
entry registration as from December&nbsp;13, 2023 and of services rendered and/or accrued as from such date. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The aforementioned measures adopted by
the Argentine Government will be financially supported by a new Extended Facilities Facility (&#147;EFF&#148;) agreed with the International Monetary Fund (&#147;IMF&#148;). In this regard, on March&nbsp;11, 2025, through DNU No.&nbsp;179/2025, the
PEN approved to enter into a new EFF with the IMF, which was approved by the Chamber of Deputies of the Argentine Congress on March&nbsp;19, 2025. On April&nbsp;8 and April&nbsp;11, 2025, the IMF and the Argentine Government, respectively, announced
that they had reached an agreement on a comprehensive economic program based on a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">4-year</FONT> EFF for a total of US$ 20&nbsp;billion, which includes quarterly reviews of targets. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Export Increase Program</U> </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;14, 2025,
Decree No.&nbsp;269/2025 repealed the Export Increase Program and as from such date the proceeds from the export of goods and services, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">pre-export</FONT> financings, post- export financings and advance payments must
be settled 100% through the Foreign Exchange Market within a general term of 20 days. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.j) Decree of Necessity and Urgency (&#147;DNU&#148; by
its acronym in Spanish) No.&nbsp;70/2023 </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, there were no significant updates to the
regulatory framework described in Note 36.i) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.k) Law of Bases and Starting Points for the
Freedom of Argentines No.&nbsp;27,742 (&#147;Bases Law&#148;) and Regulatory Decree No 1,057/2024 (&#147;Decree No 1,057/2024&#148;) </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">During the
three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025, there were no significant updates to the regulatory framework described in Note 36.j) to the annual consolidated financial statements. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The dates indicated correspond to the date of publication in the respective Official Gazettes, unless otherwise indicated. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>36.l) CNV regulatory framework </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Information

statements, the Company is registered in the CNV under the category &#147;Settlement and Clearing Agent and Trading Agent - Direct Participant&#148;, record No.&nbsp;549. Considering the Company&#146;s business and the CNV Rules, the Company will
not, under any circumstance, offer brokerage services to third parties for transactions in markets under the jurisdiction of the CNV, and it will also not open operating accounts to third parties to issue orders and trade in markets under the
jurisdiction of the CNV. </P>

<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>38. EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note 38 to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the main characteristics and accounting treatment for employee benefit plans and
similar obligations implemented by the Group. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Retirement plan</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the Retirement Plan was 1,400 and 753 for the three-month periods ended March&nbsp;31, 2025 and 2024,
respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Short-term benefit programs</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense related to the short-term benefit programs was 45,383 and 12,826 for the three-month periods ended March&nbsp;31, 2025 and
2024, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><U>Share-based benefit plans</U> </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of March&nbsp;31, 2025, there are 4.6&nbsp;million number of PSARs outstanding with and a weighted average fair value of US$ 20.77 per PSARs. The
amount charged to expense in relation with Value Generation Plan was a recovery due to changes in the fair value estimate of the option of 604 for the three-month period ended March&nbsp;31, 2025. As of December&nbsp;31, 2024, weighted average fair
value was US$ 28.6 per PSARs. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">The amount charged to expense in relation with the remaining share-based benefit plans was 2,770 and 754 to be settled
in equity instruments, and 197 and 2,872 to be settled in cash, for the three-month periods ended March&nbsp;31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">Note
2.b.11) to the annual consolidated financial statements describes the accounting policies for share-based benefit plans. Repurchases of treasury shares are disclosed in Note 32. </P>

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify"><B>40. SUBSEQUENT EVENTS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;9, 2025, the Company issued additional Class&nbsp;XXX NO for US$ 204&nbsp;million maturing in July 2026 at an issue price of 96.5% of
nominal value. The integration of additional Class&nbsp;XXX NO was made in kind through the delivery of Class&nbsp;XXIII NO for US$ 39&nbsp;million and in cash for US$ 165&nbsp;million. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On May&nbsp;6, 2025, the Company announced the results of the tender of the Class&nbsp;XXXVII NO denominated and payable in U.S. dollars maturing in May
2027, having accepted offers for US$ 140&nbsp;million at a fixed nominal annual interest rate of 7%. The Class&nbsp;XXXVII NO will be issued and integrated in U.S. dollars on May&nbsp;7, 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">On April&nbsp;2, 2025, a Memorandum of Understanding (&#147;MOU&#148;) was signed with the Province of Santa Cruz and Fomicruz S.E. for the purpose of
establishing the general terms and conditions upon which the assignment to the latter of the exploitation concessions &#147;Cerro Piedra - Cerro Guadal Norte&#148;, &#147;Barranca Yankowsky&#148;, &#147;Los Monos&#148;, &#147;El Guadal - Lomas del
Cuy&#148;, &#147;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Vasco&#148;, &#147;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Yatel&#148;, &#147;Pico Truncado - El Cord&oacute;n&#148;, &#147;Los Perales - Las Mesetas&#148;, &#147;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n Le&oacute;n - Meseta Espinosa&#148;,
&#147;Ca&ntilde;ad&oacute;n de la Escondida - Las Heras&#148; and the transportation concessions associated with such concessions will be negotiated. The MOU, subject to the approval by YPF&#146;s Board of Directors and the issuance of the
corresponding provincial decree, was approved by YPF&#146;s Board of Directors on April&nbsp;9, 2025, and issued Provincial Decree No.&nbsp;376/2025 on May&nbsp;6, 2025. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">As of the date of issuance of these condensed interim consolidated financial statements, there have been no other significant subsequent events whose
effect on Group&#146;s financial position, results of operations or their disclosure in notes to the financial statements for the period ended as of March&nbsp;31, 2025, should have been considered in said financial statements under IFRS. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL" ALIGN="justify">These condensed interim consolidated financial statements were approved by the Board of Directors&#146; meeting and authorized to be issued on May&nbsp;7,
2025. </P>
